column1: # clues.tsv for ft_isalnum -- pedagogic hints only: each line is a QUESTION, never the expected value or the fix.
# Format: <hint><TAB><CASE label><TAB>...   (a line fires if ANY of its cases fails)
man isalnum says its class is made of two other classes: which ones, and which codes does man ascii give each? What does p.8 say a classification function returns for a character in its class?
Which characters sit just outside each range in man ascii: around '0' and '9', 'A' and 'Z', 'a' and 'z'? Is one of your bounds off by one?

man ascii lists 128 characters, the last one 0x7f: is a code above it in any class of the "C" locale, the one a program runs in until it calls setlocale()? (man 3 toupper, NOTES, says what that locale knows of umlauts.) Does your class have an upper end, and does your function check it?
Which value does <stdio.h> give EOF, and is that value the code of any character?
Which codes in man ascii are neither letters nor digits? Does one of them get into your class?
Does ft_isalnum call other functions of your library? If it does, are their own suites green, and does what they return reach your caller as p.8 says it must?
